tool_input.command: cat package.json | grep -A5 scripts; npm test 2>&1 | tail -30

result:
I couldn't run the tests because `npm test` needs approval and the request wasn't granted, so the change is untested.

`GET /orders` in `src/app.ts` now returns an `items` array on each order. It's built in the same query by joining `order_items` and `products`. Each item has `product_id`, `product_name`, `quantity` and `price_cents`. Orders with no items get `[]`. Items are sorted by product id, and the order list is still limited to the caller's own orders.

I kept snake_case field names to match the existing `total_cents` and `created_at`. `price_cents` is the price stored on the order line, not the product's current price.

I also added a test in `test/app.test.ts` that checks each order has an `items` array with exactly those four fields, and that at least one order has items. To run it, use `npm test`. It needs the database to be set up and seeded.
